text: ResStock workflow Accessing and processing public ResStock data The following section outlines the steps to access and preprocess the most recent ResStock data release, in this case the 2024.2 ResStock dataset,8 to get a representative sample of all the buildings in PBC. 6 https://resstock.nrel.gov 7 https://www.nrel.gov/docs/fy22osti/80889.pdf 8 https://resstock.nrel.gov/datasets 2 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. 1. Navigate to the 2024.2 ResStock dataset website. 2. Click the ‘metadata_and_annual_results’ hyperlink for the data released in March 2024 using the AMY 2018 weather year (Figure 2). The hyperlink will be directed to a data repository in DOE’s Open Energy Data Initiative (OEDI). Figure 2: ‘metadata_and_annual_results’ link location on ResStock public data site 3. Navigate to the ‘by_state’ folder (Figure 3). Figure 3: 'by_state' folder location on the OEDI website 3 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. 4. Navigate to the ‘state=FL’ folder (Figure 4). 5. Note: The full OEDI file path is (‘oedi-data-lake/nrel-pds-building-stock/end-use-load- profiles-for-us-building- stock/2024/resstock_amy2018_release_2/metadata_and_annual_results/by_state/state=FL/’) Figure 4: 'state-FL/' folder location on the OEDI website 6. This folder contains two sub-folders, ‘csv’ and ‘parquet,’ with data stored in two data formats, .csv and .parquet file types, respectively. The files in the ‘csv’ folder can all be downloaded locally and opened in Microsoft Excel. Note: The .parquet file type is used to store large amounts tabular data in a structured data format, similar to Microsoft Excel, but with much less storage space. The ‘.parquet’ files cannot be opened by Microsoft Excel in their original form but must be preprocessed first. The files in the ‘parquet’ folder can be analyzed using a programming language, like Python or R, and the use of an integrated development environment (IDE) such as Jupyter Notebook or Visual Studio Code (VSCode) to be processed. These datasets are complex. For simple analyses, Excel may be best. However, given the complexity of the ResStock data, for tailored, multi-dimensional analyses it may be easier to use a programming language in an IDE. Instructions on how to begin processing data in the ‘parquet’ file format using Python are available in Appendix A of this document. 7. Navigate to the ‘csv’ folder. 8. Download the ‘FL_baseline_metadata_and_annual_results.csv’ file from in the and save this file into an appropriate folder. 9. Use the ‘in.county_name’ column to filter for the dwelling units in ‘Palm Beach County” Note: Each row in this .csv file is a representative housing unit, or a modeled sample of a housing unit. It does not represent a real building that exists in PBC, but rather a statistical distribution of housing likely to be found in that area.
